questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the lane position where other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit while passing.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started passing in a legal zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the posted speed limit when passing. Only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger should hold onto the motorcycle's passenger handgrips or hold your waist or hips—not just grab the back of the bike. Your motorcycle will handle differently with a passenger, so ride slower and allow more stopping distance.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together when you stop.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
It is okay for a motorcyclist to weave between lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Other drivers may change lanes, open doors, or put their arms out the window. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: If you will carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure changes.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of air pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and try to hit it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: What is the maximum engine size for a moped?

options.text: 10 cubic centimeters
20 cubic centimeters
50 cubic centimeters

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 cubic centimeters
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, a moped can have an engine no larger than 50 cubic centimeters.

questions.question: What is a primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road while trying to avoid another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A primary cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve or turn. This can cause your motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles go slower than 25 mph, like farm equipment or construction vehicles.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If danger requires you to brake and swerve, do these actions one at a time. Do not brake while swerving because this can make your motorcycle fall over.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to directional changes:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle respond more slowly to your movements. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. This sign warns you about road conditions. This sign tells you that a divided roadway is coming.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides good grip for riding, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good grip for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip of the road can be oily but usually has enough grip for safe riding, unless it rains. The oily strip is usually about two feet wide. You can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Someone is following you too closely.
You will be slowing suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light when you slow or stop so others will see that you are slowing down. This is very important if you slow faster than others expect.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, ride with caution. Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can respond quickly if needed.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, less experienced riders should be near the front behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can guide the way and watch the inexperienced riders.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: Small vehicles look ________ and slower than they actually are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle is, such as a motorcycle. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: When riding over rough pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding over rough pavement in a work zone, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, riders should be in:

options.text: A single-file formation.
Pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Generally, groups should ride in a staggered formation. Change to a single-file formation when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Must ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete passing within the posted speed limit. Only pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and traveling straight, even with a locked rear wheel.
